newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Kinnevik says Millicom to list Asian operations.
newsitem.headline: Kinnevik says Millicom to list Asian operations.

text.p: Swedish investment and media company Kinnevik said on Tuesday its partly owned MIC expected to return a portion of the proceeds to shareholders through a share repurchase or other form of distribution, Kinnevik said in a statement.
MIC would also initiate dicussions with potential strategic partners, investors, and/or buyers for its Latin American operations.
The remaining MIC business would be renamed MILLICOM S.A. and would continue to grow and develop.
It would also make an exchange or tender offer for its existing subordinated loan notes, it said.
"We consider that there is substantial value within MIC's operations which is currently not reflected in the company's stock price," said Jay Metcalfe, president and chief exeuctive of MIC.

"This plan has, as its objective, the unlocking of these values. The plan will allow investors to clearly evaluate each part of the business and will establish independant valuations for the major areas of activity."

"It is envisaged that the above transactions will be undertaken in 1997, that the issuance of shares in (Asian operations) Sanbao will be tax free to shareholders and that the other transactions will be completed on a substantially tax free basis to MIC."
MIC will seek a separate listing of its Asian cellular operating company to be called Sanbao Telecommunications through a spin-off to MIC shareholders.
In 1996, MIC Asia had annual revenues of $79.41 million and cellular operating profits before depreciation and amortisation of $17.24 million.
Subject to market conditions, Sanbao would plan to raise financing in the high yield debt market. It would seek a listing on NASDAQ in the U.S. and on a major Asian stock exchange.
